newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-House of Fraser provisions are one-off.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-House of Fraser provisions are one-off.

text.p: Troubled stores group House of Fraser Plc announced hefty losses on Thursday but said sales were up in the current year as it tries to get back into fashion with customers and ruled out any more provisions.
The British department store chain said the annual profits were hit by restructuring costs but added current sales were in line with expectations.
"We are very confident that we have got sufficient (provisions) to cover the full restructuring programme," chief executive John Coleman told Reuters.

House of Fraser said pretax profits before exceptional charges of 53.2 million pounds ($86 million) were 14.8 million pounds in the year ending January 25 compared with 14.3 million pounds previously.
It paid out an unchanged total dividend of 5.5 pence.
Coleman said if the provisions were not all used, "we will hand them back as exceptional credits."
The group, which is struggling to revive flagging fortunes, said both own-bought and concession sales had seen growth on a same-store basis in the early weeks of the current year.

"We are quietly confident, quietly happy with our sales performance so far," Coleman said, adding that the chain's refurbished Leeds, northern England, store was seeing sales up 70 percent over a year ago.
Shares edged up half a penny to 165 pence, just off a year high of 166.5 pence by 0820 GMT.

"The board is confident that the actions taken to strategically refocus the business, including the launch of new ranges, coupled with improvements in operational efficiency and customer service, will provide a strong platform for sustained growth in the years ahead," the company said in a statement.
The chain's turnaround proposals included selling three stores and overhauling its 51 others.
Coleman said talks were underway on the disposals but no further store closures were planned.
The company said that same-store sales in the year were up 6.3 percent, with concession sales up 15.8 percent and sales of own-brand merchandise rising 2.5 percent.
House of Fraser will be introducing private label own-brand clothing for men and women in the autumn, Coleman said, which it hopes will prove successful.
Coleman said although the private label would be a minority of sales, "we might see (it) reaching as much as 25 percent of our fashion sales."
He said further cost savings were expected from a second phase of restructuring, after savings of 10 million pounds a year were secured in the first part.
"The objective of phase two is two-fold. It's to increase customer service and to save more money," Coleman said.
The company has performed poorly since the Fayed brothers, who own London's landmark Harrods store, floated it in 1994.
It made a first half loss of 13.6 million pounds. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
